title: For the Democrats, now comes the hard part
gist: Noah Smith argues the 2026 Democratic midterm wave — the largest in 50 years, won mostly by moderates — is fragile like 1974/76, and that Democrats must fill an ideological vacuum (he rejects leftists and Warrenites, praises Abundance but says it lacks mass appeal, and proposes FDR-style liberal nationalism) while using Congress for corruption probes and workshopping debt and AI policy ahead of 2028.

themes.theme: 2026 midterm wave: scale and historical analogues

insights.claim: The 2026 US midterms produced the biggest Democratic midterm wave in half a century, larger than the 2010 and 2018 swings, comparable only to 1974 and 1976.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A wave this size gives Democrats both chambers of Congress, raising odds of gridlock, vetoes and aggressive oversight through 2028.
insights.quote: It was the biggest midterm wave in half a century.
insights.locator: Democrats won a historic victory

insights.claim: Noah Smith argues the 1974/1976 Democratic wipeouts were followed by a GOP rebound that dominated the 1980s, so a huge midterm win does not imply durable partisan dominance.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Don't extrapolate the 2026 wave into long-term Democratic control; political-regime trades should stay hedged.
insights.quote: the GOP bounced back shortly afterwards, dominated American politics in the 1980s, and pulled the country to the right for decades
insights.locator: Wait…1974 and 1976?

insights.claim: Democrats controlling Congress after 2026 does not give them governing power because Trump can and will veto most legislation they pass, leaving them to block, spotlight and message rather than legislate.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Expect legislative gridlock through 2028; policy change comes mainly via oversight, bipartisan deals and vetoes.
insights.quote: Trump can and will veto most legislation they pass
insights.locator: Democrats now control Congress

insights.claim: Smith sees Trump tracking the 2006 pattern, where a lame-duck midterm wave preceded the opposition winning the presidency, while noting 2010→2012 and 2018→2020 show midterm waves don't always translate.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Raises the probability of a Democratic presidency in 2028, conditional on Trump continuing corruption and mistakes.
insights.quote: 2006 is the only modern lame-duck term with a wave like this
insights.locator: That’s possible to do, especially

themes.theme: Moderates, not the left, won the wave

insights.claim: The 2026 Democratic wave was won overwhelmingly by moderates; the Blue Dog Coalition added at least 14 members, nearly doubling in size, and New Democrats and Problem Solvers also grew.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A centrist-heavy Democratic caucus makes bipartisan deals (e.g., permitting, housing) more plausible than leftist agendas.
insights.quote: had added at least 14 to its ranks, nearly doubling in size
insights.locator: This was a center-left victory

insights.claim: Part of moderates' outperformance is mechanical: leftists win by primarying moderates in deep-blue seats, while bigger waves deliver more swing seats, which moderates win.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Read faction strength through seat composition, not just headline wave size.
insights.locator: Some of this is purely mechanical.

insights.claim: Ballot results signaled rejection of leftist policies: biological-sex restrictions in schools passed with healthy margins and DSA-backed slates in San Francisco were wiped out.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Cultural-left policy is politically weak even in a blue wave; expect Democrats to avoid it.

insights.claim: California voters rejected the billionaire tax and approved a competing ballot proposition forbidding such taxes in the future, which Smith attributes to the tax being extreme and poorly designed.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Reduces wealth-tax risk in California for high-net-worth individuals and tech founders; shows voters' limit on taxing the rich.
insights.quote: they approved a competing ballot proposition forbidding such taxes in the future
insights.locator: Second, their policies tend to be

insights.claim: 52% of midterm voters said support for trans rights has gone too far versus 26% saying not far enough, which Smith reads as the 2010s 'woke' wave continuing to recede.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Cultural-issue positioning by Democrats likely shifts to the center ahead of 2028.
insights.quote: 52% of midterm voters say support for trans rights has gone too far vs. 26% saying not far enough
insights.locator: There are two parts of the basic story

insights.claim: Swing voters have re-emerged: young white men went from favoring Trump by 28 points in 2024 to favoring Democrats by about 17 points in 2026 per CNN exit polls.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Electorate is unusually volatile; party coalitions are fluid, increasing 2028 outcome uncertainty.
insights.quote: Democrats won young white men tonight by 17 points, per CNN exits
insights.locator: Second, voters have not yet embraced

insights.claim: Prominent 2026 Democratic winners ran on centrist positions — e.g., El-Sayed tough on the border, Talarico pro-oil and gas, Andrews a deficit hawk, Acton wanting tax cuts.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Pro-oil-and-gas and fiscally hawkish Democrats lower the policy risk premium on energy and taxes.

themes.theme: The Democrats' ideological vacuum and competing factions

insights.claim: Smith argues most Democratic and Dem-leaning voters are simply anti-Trump with no vision for governing, and that 'Resistance Liberalism' became headless once the woke identity framing of Trump's first term ended.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Without a program, a Democratic return to power risks ineffective governance and continued backlash cycles.
insights.quote: Right now, the problem with Resistance Liberalism is that it’s headless.
insights.locator: Right now, my assessment is that most

insights.claim: Smith expects the leftist faction (El-Sayed, Mamdani, Sanders) to fail to lead the Democrats because it is factional, overreaches on policy, allies with bad causes, and is itself very woke.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Lower odds of a socialist-led Democratic platform in 2028.
insights.quote: These shortcomings ought to prove fatal to the leftists’ chances of taking over the American left
insights.locator: The leftists are organized, purposeful

insights.claim: Smith says the Warrenite New Antitrust movement got little done under Biden and picked the wrong target, since Americans aren't very mad at Zuckerberg or Bezos being rich, and AI disrupted the FAANG business models they attacked.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Big Tech antitrust risk from a future Democratic administration may be lower than feared.
insights.quote: Years of frothing with rage against Mark Zuckerberg and the old FAANG companies just ended up looking silly when AI came along and disrupted their business models.
insights.locator: The second faction vying to take over

insights.claim: Smith expects Abundance policies, especially on housing and energy, to be implemented because elites across parties find them convincing, citing a bipartisan permitting reform bill moving through Congress — but Abundance lacks the mass political energy to lead the party.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Watch the bipartisan permitting reform bill — positive for energy, infrastructure and housing builders.
insights.quote: Abundance will win, but it will not win all the things the Democrats would need it to win.
insights.locator: Anyway, the third faction is Abundance.

insights.claim: Smith proposes FDR-style liberal nationalism — pluralistic patriotism plus national purpose — as the ethos Democrats should adopt, with figures like Jon Ossoff and James Talarico as carriers and Abundance supplying policy.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A liberal-nationalist Democratic platform would favor industrial policy and harnessing big tech to national goals over breaking it up.
insights.locator: The Democrats need something more

themes.theme: Opposition agenda: corruption probes, debt and AI

insights.claim: In the national exit poll (sample 79,668), 90% said government corruption was a crucial/major factor, edging cost of living at 89% and the Iran war at 74%.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Corruption is a top voter issue, so expect intensive congressional investigations to dominate headlines.
insights.locator: Corruption turned out to be a huge

insights.claim: House and Senate Democrats plan subpoena-backed probes into Trump family business dealings, the Epstein investigation, ICE operations, the White House ballroom, mineral deals, DC real estate and crypto dealings with Steve Witkoff.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Headline and legal risk for Trump-linked crypto ventures, mineral deals and real-estate projects in 2027-28.
insights.quote: his crypto dealings with special envoy Steve Witkoff
insights.locator: Even in opposition, Democrats can

insights.claim: Smith identifies the out-of-control national debt and AI as America's two big looming economic challenges, and argues Democrats should use their congressional majority to workshop policies for both before 2028.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Fiscal consolidation and AI-labor policy are likely central 2028 platform planks.
insights.locator: What they can also do is to workshop

insights.claim: Smith argues full deficit-reduction budgets would be vetoed and Trump praised for it, so Democrats should push partial measures like sunsetting the Trump tax cuts on pass-through businesses.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Pass-through tax treatment is a likely Democratic target; relevant for self-employed and private-business owners.
insights.quote: Sunsetting the Trump tax cuts on pass-through businesses is one good idea
insights.locator: The debt is actually the much harder

insights.claim: Smith recommends Democrats propose AI-disruption protections for workers such as flexible welfare programs, employment incentives and social wealth funds, testing which are popular for the 2028 platform.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Social wealth funds and AI labor policies could become mainstream Democratic proposals, affecting AI firms' regulatory environment.
insights.locator: AI is ultimately the thornier policy
